interpretation.whatHappenedAtX: The one validator started WITHOUT the transition computed a different state at block 300 (reward 2 SUR vs 3 SUR) and rejected the canonical block 300 as invalid (state root mismatch); it dropped out of consensus. It did not fork the chain: it produced no accepted block after 300.
interpretation.networkBehavior: The four healthy validators (exactly the QBFT quorum of 4/5) continued without a halt. Block 300 itself was produced on time; blocks 301, 305, 309, ... show a 13 s gap (3 s + one 10 s request-timeout round change) -- the slots in which the missing validator was the round-0 proposer.
interpretation.caveat: node5 later died with java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space. All nodes ran with the test-wide -Xmx512m cap, so this may be an artifact of the cap interacting with the repeated failed-sync loop; it is NOT established that Besu terminates on its own in this situation with a normal heap.
interpretation.consequence: With f=1 already consumed, any second fault would halt the chain (no quorum). A one-node configuration mismatch is survivable but visibly degrades block time (~+10 s every 4th block) until fixed.
